sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Package setup and root commands
sections.what: Defines the root package rules, the install guard, the build and type-check commands, and the local setup commands. It also sets the required Node.js version.
sections.why: Gives developers one consistent set of commands for the whole project.
sections.watch_out: The install guard deletes the npm and yarn lock files without asking, so any work saved only in them is lost.

summary: The root package file for the whole project. It defines the root commands for building, type-checking, and local setup, and it requires Node.js 22 or newer.
purpose: The entry point for the root commands developers run.
why: Likely reason: root commands coordinate the whole workspace. The preinstall rule that forces pnpm is stated in the code.
how: The preinstall step blocks installs that do not use pnpm and deletes the npm and yarn lock files. The build command runs the type check, then builds every package. The typecheck command checks the libraries, then the artifacts and scripts. The local commands set up the environment, create the schema, seed data, and start the dev servers.
inputs: None directly. Read by pnpm and by the developer.
risks: The preinstall step deletes package-lock.json and yarn.lock without asking. The engine rule rejects older Node.js versions.
debug: If install says to use pnpm, switch to pnpm. If the build fails at typecheck, run typecheck:libs first to isolate the library error. If the engine check fails, upgrade Node.js.
